title: Did Jatayu Really Appear in Kanpur?
description:
Indian news media recently claimed that Jatayu—the mythological bird from the Ramayana—was spotted in Kanpur, just 200 km from Ayodhya. Anchors confidently called it a divine “avatar,” turning the sighting of a Himalayan Vulture into a religious spectacle. Using clips and sensational headlines, they manipulated viewers into believing myth over evidence.

In reality, the bird shown was the Himalayan Vulture (Himalayan Griffon), one of the largest vultures in the world with a wingspan up to 8.5 feet. These birds live across the Indian subcontinent and Tibet, and are listed as Near Threatened due to habitat loss and poisoning from livestock drugs like diclofenac. Instead of celebrating conservation, the media sold superstition.

This video exposes how religious myths get injected into newsrooms, how blind faith overrides scientific temper, and why the Indian Constitution itself reminds us to cultivate skepticism and reason. If you’ve searched for Jatayu spotted in India, Himalayan Vulture mistaken for Jatayu, Ramayana bird myth, media sensationalism India, or religion vs science in news, this video gives you the rational perspective.

Don’t forget to subscribe, like, comment, and share — hype this video so it reaches more people and sparks better conversations!

00:00 – Jatayu spotted? Media’s shocking claim
02:20 – How anchors manipulate faith with myths
05:10 – The truth: Himalayan Vulture explained
09:00 – Why this bird is mistaken for Jatayu
12:30 – Conservation issues: habitat loss & diclofenac
16:20 – Religion, media, and superstition in India
